# #1721: Patch: patches check validates the technical changelog it ships
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The public Patch Notes page renders a committed changelog file. That file is validated only at the moment an entry is appended — never re-checked afterwards — so a hand edit, a duplicate entry, or a version that no longer exists slips straight onto the public page. After the change, the repository's patch-file check re-validates the whole file on every run, like every other generated artifact beside it.

## Why

`read_technical` only parses (`crates/tools/src/technical.rs:203-210`); `patches log` validates entries at append (`line_problems`, :282-288). `patches check` covers pending fragments, snapshots, carried versions and win-rate blobs (`patches.rs:1409-1520, 1746-1826`) — `technical.json` is absent. The web renders it publicly (`apps/web/src/patches/source.ts`, `PatchNotes.tsx`, `routes/patch-notes.tsx`), so a bad entry ships to users — an asymmetry: it is the one shipped artifact in `patches/` without a committed-state check.

## Proposal

Add `check_technical(entries, patches_json) -> Vec<String>` wired into `check_patches`: unique commits, each `version` present in `patches.json`, valid `kind`s, `pr` shape, and `player` lines passing R724001's readability rule — mirroring `check_fragments`.

## Where it lands

`crates/tools/src/technical.rs`, `crates/tools/src/patches.rs`, with fixture tests alongside the existing fragment/carried tests (`patches.rs:4479+`). Spec §9.x patch-notes surface; R724001.

## Acceptance criteria

- Fixtures with a duplicate commit, a version missing from `patches.json`, an invalid kind, or an unreadable player line each fail.
- The committed `technical.json` passes today — or the change fixes it in the same pull request.
- `cargo jackioh patches check` covers it in CI.

## Size and risks

Small. Pure function plus fixtures, in exactly the style the file already uses.
